# Sizing a power station for a fridge

You need to check three numbers, and a station has to pass all of them.

1. **Surge watts: at least 1,300 W.** The compressor spikes at startup, typically 1,000-2,400 W depending on the fridge. This is the spec that most often disqualifies small units, however much battery they have. ([BlackBox Supplies](https://www.blackboxsupplies.com/guides/what-size-power-station-to-run-a-refrigerator-in-a-power-outage), [PowerStations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/power-station-for-a-refrigerator))
2. **Continuous watts: about 300 W or more.** A full-size fridge runs at roughly 100-250 W, so almost any 1,000 W-class station clears this. Choose a pure sine wave inverter. ([BlackBox Supplies](https://www.blackboxsupplies.com/guides/what-size-power-station-to-run-a-refrigerator-in-a-power-outage))
3. **Watt-hours: depends on outage length.** The compressor only runs about 30-40% of the time, so a fridge averages roughly 40-65 W, or about 1,000-1,500 Wh per day after inverter losses. ([HomeGrid HQ](https://www.homegridhq.com/watts/fridge/))

## Capacity by outage length

| Outage | Battery size |
|---|---|
| About 12-17 hours | About 1,000 Wh |
| 24 hours | About 1,400-2,000 Wh |
| 2 days | About 2,800 Wh |
| 3 days | About 4,200 Wh |

These figures come from [HomeGrid HQ](https://www.homegridhq.com/watts/fridge/) and [PowerStations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/power-station-for-a-refrigerator). A 1,000 Wh unit like the Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 is estimated at about 17 hours.

To tailor this to your fridge, find the kWh/year on its yellow EnergyGuide label. Multiply by 1,000 and divide by 8,760 to get average watts. Then multiply by the hours you need, divide by 0.85 for inverter losses, and add about 20% headroom. Large side-by-sides with ice makers can use double the typical figure, and warm kitchens and frequent door openings raise it too. Keeping the door shut helps a lot.

## Options that pass the surge check

- **Day-long backup (~1,000-1,150 Wh):** The [BLUETTI AC180](https://www.blackboxsupplies.com/guides/what-size-power-station-to-run-a-refrigerator-in-a-power-outage) has 1,152 Wh, 1,800 W output and 2,700 W peak, and was recently seen at $399-699. The Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 is also in this class, at about $449-799 in the same guide.
- **A full day or more (~2,000 Wh):** The [Anker SOLIX S2000](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/portable-power-station-for-refrigerator) has 2,010 Wh, 1,500 W output and 3,000 W peak, listed at $699.99 after coupon. The [BLUETTI AC200L](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac200l) has 2,048 Wh, 2,400 W output, and expands up to 8,192 Wh. It lists at $899, or $854.05 with code AFF5OFF. That is an affiliate link, and the code was tested in BLUETTI's cart on 2026-10-21.

If you want a day of backup with margin, or to run a few other things like a router or lights, aim for about 2,000 Wh. If you only need to bridge a short outage, about 1,000 Wh is enough. Prices change often, so confirm at checkout.

Before an outage, test the fridge on the station. If it trips at startup, unplug other AC loads and retry. A repeated trip means the surge rating is too low.
